Result: 19/19 PASS. Live response for carlos@lasalud.gt: role=clinic_admin, sales_today=Q5240/12, ar_pending=Q1220, low_stock=0, expiring=0, expenses_month=Q3136, commissions_month=Q600, open_cash_sessions=2, 1 ar_overdue alert (severity=danger), 26-point income_chart from 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-26, my_commissions_month=null. action_items: Doctor-role frontend testing was NOT executed (no pre-seeded doctor user) — covered by code review only. Backend unit tests for doctor branch (my_commissions_month populated, scoped today_appointments/rx_issued_month) were also not exercised live; recommend creating a temporary doctor member in a future iteration, or a unit test via pytest with a mocked ctx.
Optional code-review nit: appointments.py:419 has dead code 'ar_ids = [a.get('id') for a in ar_rows] if False else None' — remove the obsolete branch.

Optional: 'expiring' alert message says '60 días' but the cutoff in the SQL is 'expiration_date < now+60d' which also matches batches that are already expired. Consider splitting into 'expired' (severity=danger) and 'expiring' (severity=warning). Currently 0 in test clinic so not user-visible.
critical_code_review_comments: appointments.py:419 — dead conditional 'ar_ids = [...] if False else None' is confusing; the value is then re-fetched two lines below. Clean-up suggested.

appointments.py — for each today's appointment and each recent activity, the code issues N+1 Supabase round-trips to fetch patient/doctor names (loops at lines 56-67, 310-323, 328-344, 347-353). Works for small clinics but will scale poorly. Consider a single .in_('id', [...]) query and a dict lookup. Same pattern appears in list_appointments.

appointments.py — get_clinic_features is called once at the top; good. But the inventory low_stock_count loop at 444-456 issues one inventory_stock query per product (N+1). Could be replaced by a single query with a server-side aggregate or by joining batches.

appointments.py — Income chart re-uses the existing /sales table with status filter; this duplicates logic already in /api/clinic/sales/daily-summary. Consider extracting a shared helper to avoid drift between dashboard and reports.

ClinicDashboardPage.js — 615 lines is right at the recommended 700-line cap; if more cards are added, split AdminStatsRow/AlertsCard/IncomeChartCard/MyCommissionsCard/CashSessionCard into separate files under /pages/clinic/dashboard/.

ClinicDashboardPage.js:319-329 — useCallback's deps array is empty but uses 'headers' from getAuthHeaders() at component scope; the eslint-disable comment masks this. Token rotation while the dashboard is open would not refresh the request header. Acceptable now (60s polling will get the new token after re-mount) but worth noting.

ClinicDashboardPage.js — alert-* data-testid uses alert.type as suffix; if two alerts share the same type (e.g., two cash_session warnings) testids will collide. Backend currently de-dupes by 'break', so OK in practice.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing clinic data. Live values: sales_today=Q5240, ar_pending=Q1220, expenses=Q3136, commissions=Q600, 2 open cash sessions, 1 ar_overdue.
context_for_next_testing_agent: PROMPT A9 dashboard is fully functional and visually verified for clinic_admin (carlos@lasalud.gt). All 13 review-request assertions PASS. Doctor-role and assistant/receptionist front-desk paths are NOT yet covered with live tests because no such pre-seeded users exist in the test clinic — to add coverage, create temp clinic_member rows with role=doctor / role=receptionist, then re-run /api/clinic/dashboard with their tokens to verify (a) doctor sees only their own today_appointments/next_appointment/rx_issued_month, (b) doctor admin_stats is empty, (c) doctor my_commissions_month is populated when they have commissions, (d) front-desk sees CashSessionCard. Backend unit-test alternatives can stub require_clinic_member ctx to inject role/member_id. The new test file at /app/backend/tests/test_dashboard_prompt_a9.py is the smoke gate for any future dashboard changes.
rca of the issue: No bugs found in PROMPT A9 implementation. Code review notes captured above are forward-looking improvements, not regressions.
